Definition: properly, lax, i.e. (figuratively) a ghost (as dead; in plural only)
BiblicalUsage: Rapha' is the shades — the dead, the ghosts of the departed, properly the lax and feeble ones. Isaiah says, 'Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead'; and again, 'They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise'; Proverbs says the simple man 'knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell'; and the psalm asks, 'Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee?'
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that the shades teach me what death is without God: the dead are feeble, they cannot praise, they dwell in the depths — and that is why Isaiah's promise is everything: 'Thy dead men shall live.' And I hold that the same word that names the hopeless dead also carries the hope: the earth shall cast out the dead, and they shall arise.
